title: A world in a leaf
text: Tea began as a medicine in southwest China, became the everyday drink of an empire, and then {{1}} the world economy to a degree few plants have matched. Reaching Britain in the seventeenth century as a luxury for the rich, it was soon the national drink, {{2}} by duchesses and dock workers alike. The hunger for leaves had {{3}} consequences: since China wanted little in {{4}} except silver, British merchants balanced the books by selling opium, a commerce that produced two wars. Determined to break the Chinese {{5}}, the East India Company sent the botanist Robert Fortune, who in 1848 travelled the country in disguise and smuggled out thousands of seedlings and, just as {{6}}, an entire team of experienced tea-makers; the Indian tea industry began with his cargo. Tea also rewired British daily life: the working day grew an afternoon {{7}}, 'taking tea' became a social ceremony with its own etiquette, and phrases like 'for all the tea in China' entered the language. Few commodities can {{8}} such a record — medicine, currency of empire, cause of war, and finally the modest cup that cheers.

gaps.explanation: 'then reshaped the world economy' — changed its structure; resound = echo, retreat = withdraw.
'the national drink, drunk by duchesses and dock workers' — the passive participle is needed, not the past tense 'drank'.
'had far-reaching consequences' — extending widely in effect; far-fetched = implausible, far-sighted = wise, far-flung = distant.
'little in exchange except silver' — 'in exchange' = in return; expense takes 'at', excess takes 'in excess of'.
'break the Chinese monopoly' — exclusive control of the tea trade; the other mono- nouns are unrelated.
'just as crucially, an entire team of tea-makers' — of equal decisive importance; casually = without care, courteously = politely.
'the working day grew an afternoon pause' — a rest break; pulse = a heartbeat, purse = a small bag for money.
'few commodities can claim such a record' — can point to it as their own; exclaim = cry out, acclaim = praise.
